title: Backup Restore Failed
description: Recover when a backup restore fails — partial imports, database errors, timeout issues, and mismatched file/database restores.

steps.title: Document Restore Failure Point
steps.instructions: Note where restore stopped: database import, file extraction, search-replace, or timeout. Identify backup tool used and backup age.

steps.title: Verify Backup Archive Integrity
steps.instructions: Confirm backup zip is not corrupted (re-download, check file size). Test extracting on local machine. Try an older backup if recent one is damaged.

steps.title: Raise PHP and Server Limits for Restore
steps.instructions: Increase max_execution_time, memory_limit, and upload_max_filesize. Large restores should use WP-CLI, SSH, or host restore tool instead of browser.

steps.title: Restore Database and Files Separately
steps.instructions: If combined restore fails, import SQL via phpMyAdmin or WP-CLI first, then upload files via SFTP. Match backup date for both halves.

steps.title: Run URL Search-Replace After Restore
steps.instructions: Restoring to different domain requires serialization-safe search-replace. Use Better Search Replace or wp search-replace --dry-run first.

steps.title: Fix File Permissions After Restore
steps.instructions: Restored files may have wrong ownership. Set directories 755, files 644. Ensure wp-config.php is readable but not world-writable.

steps.title: Try Alternative Restore Method
steps.instructions: If plugin restore fails, try host snapshot restore, WP-CLI import, or manual SQL + SFTP. All-in-One WP Migration may need unlimited extension for large sites.

steps.title: Verify Restored Site Completely
steps.instructions: Test homepage, admin login, media, forms, and checkout. Compare post count and media count to pre-disaster baseline if available.
